request.name: Non-ingestive food usefulness and hazard assessment
request.function: Determine what physically supported, non-ingestive tests could establish nutritional usefulness or detect hazards in my actual tuber sample. Distinguish measured results from unresolved hazards; do not treat a negative limited test as universal safety.
request.conditions: At tick 330 I hold a tuber sample gathered from forest-tuber-0 and a retained opened portion item-329-sol-2041. Paid internal examination found little observable deterioration but explicitly did not establish nutrition, digestibility or toxin absence. Root and berry are personally known safe foods. Existing relative drying measurements do not establish chemical safety.
request.inputs: Actual retained tuber portions; any additional reference materials or apparatus must first be identified and physically obtained. Suitable methods and dependencies are unknown.
request.costs: Unknown; specify real material, energy, time and reference requirements before testing. Do not require tasting an unknown sample.
request.effects: Provide a feasible evidence-limited testing pathway, or explain the missing independently verifiable prerequisites if no such assessment is currently implementable. No automatic edibility certificate, detoxification or nutrition discovery.

projects.question: Can measured short poles and tested grass components form a useful small refuge?
evidence: The two-unit cover trial completed at tick 278 and failed.
Tick 279 diagnostics identified slip 0.04132446 above the acceptance limit 0.02; intactness and sag passed.
The recorded model ties slip to applied force, grass dry mass and wetness. A different configuration remains untested.
projects.uncertainty: No passed cover configuration, tested joints or assembled refuge has been demonstrated.
projects.goal: Investigate a feasible refuge without compromising survival reserves.
outputs: Recorded specimen-specific trial response and failure predicate.
projects.missing: Fresh suitable grass, a passed cover trial, tested joints and sufficient measured poles.
projects.next: Replenish safe food before choosing further material trials.
projects.pauseReason: Only one known-safe root is currently available in personal stock; replenish provisions first.
projects.benefit: The failure is now explained; no shelter relief has been demonstrated.

projects.question: Can the existing small drying tray measurably slow deterioration of a real berry sample?
evidence: Paid calibrated readings at ticks 171 and 176 established mass loss within finite measurement resolution.
At tick 176 the surviving batch demonstrated lower deterioration during the observed exposure.
projects.uncertainty: One small batch only. Composition assumptions, finite resolution and future weather remain uncertain; the result is not a food-safety certificate.
projects.goal: Test actual ambient preservation without compromising survival reserves.
outputs: Recorded specimen-specific evidence of mass loss and reduced deterioration.
projects.missing: No safety certification or guarantee of future storage life.
projects.next: Leave the sample undisturbed while replenishing fresh known-safe food.
projects.benefit: Reduced deterioration demonstrated for this batch under its actual elapsed exposure.

projects.question: What can calibrated relative drying measurements establish about an actual food sample?
evidence: The balance passed calibration at tick 73.
Paid readings at ticks 84 and 87 were both 0.2 with resolution 0.05.
At tick 88 the assay was invalidated because the actual sample spoiled or disappeared.
projects.uncertainty: No certified stable residue estimate, composition result, or safety conclusion was obtained.
projects.goal: Obtain a valid relative drying measurement without compromising survival reserves.
completedSteps: Constructed and calibrated a comparison balance.
Obtained two paid sample readings before invalidation.
outputs: Two relative mass readings from an invalidated assay.
projects.missing: A surviving sample and sufficient stable readings.
projects.next: Replenish known safe food before deciding whether another sample is worthwhile.
projects.pauseReason: The plum sample spoiled before assay completion.
projects.benefit: Reusable apparatus remains; no food-safety benefit was demonstrated.

{"reviews":[{"actor":"sol","decision":"develop","ability":null,"reason":"Internal examination and relative drying measurements already cover tissue condition and water loss, but neither establishes digestibility, nutritional value or toxin absence. A missing, feasible precursor is a controlled aqueous-extractability experiment with an independently performed known-food comparison. It can establish limited physical processing behavior, not food safety. Specific nutrient or hazard detection additionally requires a validated analyte-specific method, appropriate controls and physically obtained apparatus; none is established here. No tasting is required.","specification":"Implement noningestive-extractability@1 through the current conversation handoff. Reuse existing food examination, water access, calibrated weighing and drying code separately from this new experimental function. Individual prerequisites: food-assay, measured-food-preservation and access-water mastery; their existing dependencies remain applicable. No equipment, water, reference food or mastery is supplied.
Public strict schema: {mode: inspect|prepare|read|resume|cancel|remove, project:string, sample:string, reference:string, water:string, apparatus:string[], quantityTenths:integer>=0, waterMl:integer>=0}. References use exact persistent IDs or one item:/object: prefix, never resource aliases. Inspect requires an accessible subject and zero unused quantities; prepare requires distinct owned sample/reference allocations, positive quantities, actual retained water and explicitly named calibrated balance, original comparison weights, drying tray and two intact cups. Other modes name the existing personal project and leave unused fields empty/zero. Publish eligible apparatus roles, capacities and uncertainty before allocation.
Physical scope: compare actual water extraction and subsequent dried residue from unknown food and a personally evidenced known-food reference; the reference does not transfer safety. Add a versioned conservative physical partition model for root/tuber tissue: initial water fraction 0.75, with 0.20 of dry matter water-extractable. These are declared simulation assumptions, not actor measurements or nutrient identities. Preserve existing food composition, age, processing history and water already represented; initialize only previously absent fields, never overwrite measured or processed composition. Extraction moves conserved dry material between tissue and liquid, not nutrition or toxins out of existence. Unsupported composition remains unassayable until its physical model is supplied. Neither soluble nor insoluble material is automatically digestible, nutritious, harmless or detoxified.
Inspect costs one round/0.2 energy. Preparation has four attended stages at 0.5 energy each: baseline weighing, water allocation, mixing/contact, and physical separation into the tray. Each arm needs water mass at least twice allocated dry mass and must fit actual cup/tray capacity. Both arms receive separately allocated materials and paid handling. Contact requires two elapsed rounds after mixing; extraction approaches its modeled limit by half the remaining extractable amount per wet round. Separation transfers only actual free liquid and suspended material, retaining measured transfer losses. No filter, sterile vessel, heating or selective chemistry is implied. Cups retain their existing leakage, wall erosion and collapse behavior. Leaked solids and clay contamination enter located deposits or retained mixtures; unmeasured contamination or losses can invalidate an extractability estimate. Residue drying uses existing weather, tray occupancy and deterioration mechanisms. Each read costs 0.2 energy plus existing weighing costs for every actual weighing. Report interval estimates; a quantitative conclusion requires two paid stable residue readings, supported baseline measurements and differences exceeding combined uncertainty. Otherwise return an inconclusive result with the actual limiting factor.
Persist exact allocations, composition lineage, apparatus identities, location, elapsed contact, measurements, uncertainty, paid stages, remaining work and owner. Use shared interaction reach 0.65, actual clear access segments, apparatus collision geometry and geometric capacities. No remote transfers or virtual surfaces. Insufficient energy/access pauses attended work without charge; weather, spoilage and cup leakage continue physically. Resume executes only remaining work. Completion is terminal; repetition creates a newly paid allocation. Cancellation or death terminates the controller and releases surviving escrow once at its actual location, retaining mixtures, damage and provenance; never clone, erase or refund consumed material. Installed passive material persists without an active owner controller.
Declare extraction-inspected, extraction-progress, extraction-reading, extraction-completed, extraction-invalidated and extraction-stopped for validated subscriptions. Completion records measured extractability only, unresolved nutritional and hazard questions, and method limitations. Specific hazard tests must remain unavailable until a concrete physical detection mechanism, independently checkable positive/negative controls, sensitivity and interference limits exist; no generic hazard-screen result. Preserve historical records and register new schemas and physical-model revision without changing prior findings. Review and implementation advance no simulation time.","experienceReview":"The potential benefit is understanding gained from a successful experiment, not edibility reassurance or mastery. Subscribe qualifying extraction-reading/extraction-completed events to the existing information-confirmed mechanism: only the performing actor, after a paid, valid measurement establishes a previously unresolved physical property beyond uncertainty, receives confirmed-understanding feedback. Reuse its single functional source: transient amount 0.8, cap 1, duration 8 rounds, refresh repetition with a 12-round cooldown; maintained gain 0.035, decay 0.0015 per round, shared cap 1, only upon qualifying continued experimentation. Deduplicate by specimen lineage, property and supported conditions across all interfaces. Existing findings, inconclusive readings, requests, learning and labels award nothing. No separate pleasure or safety-relief source is warranted by this potentially tedious and inconclusive assay; hunger, health and protected mental accounts remain unchanged.","visualReview":"Show the actual two located cups, allocated food portions, water levels, mixing and transfer progress, occupied tray regions, drying residues, leakage deposits and any clay contamination or vessel collapse. Bind presentation to the declared extraction events and existing water/drying events. Measurement overlays distinguish observed intervals, declared model assumptions and unresolved hazards; display an explicit 'not a safety or nutrition certificate' limitation. Replay retains paid stage transitions, exact transfers, losses, uncertainty and cancellation outcomes rather than depicting an automatic successful laboratory test.","learning":4}]}
